items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: He played with King Oliver a long time up there.

ctx.x: Huh? Do you remember Bobby? Oh sure. Used to call him Hard Yard. Yeah.

He was a good drummer. Yeah. He went out there to California too. You there yet? That's another, no, I heard from him. But what was he? He was a good drummer. Yeah. He went out there to California too. You there yet? He said, I don't know, I heard from him. He said, what did you see there? He said, he'd dress up feet all the time. Yeah. He was a good little drummer. He was a cheap. Every time they come on the job, he'd buy the band a pint of whiskey, a quart of whiskey. You know, whiskey was cheap then, you know.…
Boy one on his arm, one on his arm, one on his mouth, and two on his back part.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: The first lick I hit on the guitar was Joe, Joe, Oliver and old man Umphrey.

ctx.x: Ask him did he know Joe Oliver?

Did you know Joe Oliver? Oh yeah, Joe. He was on the corner from Joe Oliver. That's the time I used to go to the Royal Guard. He got that job out today. Bless you know. Yeah, he was the king out there. And then when he was older than me, he was about five or six years old than me. But I know them when they first had a band organized. There was a brother named Kintin. He had all these youngsters from fifteen to eighteen years old playing a bass band. He used to carry them all around in different places up and down…
Who was in that band? Kinkins Band or Jenkins?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: You know, the thing I got in there when I was standing right by Joe Oliver with a fellow drumming him, Buddy Sali.

ctx.x: I asked him which came first.

We had some band, too. Most of our jobs called for white people. We said. We was up three years before we could play for one color people. And the first time we played for color people when Joe Oliver left from the air. You know, the thing I got in there when I was standing right by Joe Oliver with a fellow drumming him, Buddy Sali. Hit him in the eye with a wheel by the hammer. And you know, I thought Joe would be one eye, you know. And he used to have a man, Carol, all them boys. He must have been around about…
I asked you who this Bourne was. That's not Harrison Bourne.
